strengths: Important problem: Addresses real bottlenecks in long-context LLM inference (quadratic attention, linear KV cache memory)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple benchmarks (RULER, LongBench, MileBench), model families (Qwen, Llama), with consistent improvements over strong baselines
Strong practical impact: SpecKV-PC achieves 40-75% speedup with 25GB memory savings at 64K context vs LAQ++
Thorough ablation studies: Examines draft quality, lookahead length, sparse prefilling sparsity, cross-family robustness
Solid theoretical grounding: Theorems 1-3 provide bounds on importance error; Figure 2 empirically validates theory-practice connection
Clear presentation: Well-motivated, clear algorithmic descriptions, effective visualizations, comprehensive complexity comparison (Table 1)
Reproducibility commitment: Detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, extensive appendices, promised code release
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: Theorem 1 is straightforward spectral analysis; Theorem 2 relies on strong unverified RIP assumption for embeddings; Theorem 3 bound is loose (exponential terms)
Theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes strict token alignment, but Eq. 2 uses ad-hoc centroid distance relaxation without theoretical justification
Incremental over prior work: SpecKV vs LAQ++ mainly differs in draft model choice (not conceptually novel); SpecPC extends SpecPrefill with modest gains; SpecKV-PC is straightforward combination
Dependence on draft model: Requires reasonably accurate draft model; cross-family SpecPC shows 4-5 point degradation; no principled guidance for draft selection
Experimental sample sizes: Only 5 samples per RULER task, 50 from LongBench for main results; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
LAQ++ comparison: Uses authors' own implementation rather than official code, raising fairness concerns
Incomplete failure analysis: No exploration of when lookahead hurts or task-specific failure modes despite rare negative results
Missing assumptions verification: RIP assumption for Theorem 2 is unverified for actual LLM embeddings; Theorem 1 assumes ‖x_j‖₂ ≤ √d without validation
